                   Provincial Government (Preparatory Arrangements) Act
1974

                         SUSPENSION ORDER
  I JOHN GUISE, G.C.M.G., Governor-General, by virtue of the powers
conferred by Sections 9A and 9D of the
    Provincial Government (Preparatory Arrangements) Act 1974, and
all other powers me enabling, acting with,
  and in accordance with, the advice of the National Executive
Council, being of the opinion that it is in the
  national interest to do so, hereby—
      (a) order that all the powers and functions of the Provincial
Government of Bougainville be suspended;
        and
      (b) appoint the persons specified in Column 1 of the Schedule
to be the Bougainville Provincial Trust;
        and
      (c) appoint each person specified in Column 2 of the Schedule
opposite the name of a person specified
        in Column 1 to be the deputy of that person.

      (a) Of the land suitable for cultivation, the following
proportions shall be planted in a good and husbandlike manner with

          a crop/crops or pasture species of economic value, which
shall be harvested regularly in accordance with sound com-

            mercial practice:


             One half in the first period of 5 years of the term;

           Four-fifths in the first period of 10 years of the term;
and during the remainder of the term four-fifths of the land so

                suitable shall be kept so planted.


      (b) Provided always that if at the end of the first two (2)
years of the term, the lessee has not made such progress

with the land preparation and plantings as to suggest that
he will fulfil the improvement conditions, the Minister, for

          Lands after considering any reply from the lessee to a
demand to show cause why he (the Minister) should not so do

          may, by notice in the Gazette and in accordance with the
Land Act 1962, as amended to date, forfeit the Lease.


      (c) The lessee or his agent shall take up residency or
occupancy of the block within six months of date of grant.


      (d) That portion of the lease which is to be utilised for
grazing shall be stocked with a minimum of 1 head of great

          cattle per 3 ha. within 1 year from the date of grant, and
1 head of great cattle per 2 hectares within 4 years from

          the date of grant and shall be kept stocked to that
minimum for the remainder of the term.


          That portion of the lease which is to be utilised for
grazing shall within 1 year from the date of grant be fenced

          externally with a barbed wire fence of not less than four
strands having posts not more than 4.5 metres (15 feet)

          apart and strainer posts at least every 100 metres (5
chains) the said fence to be kept well strained and in stock-proof

          condition.


      (f) That portion of the lease which is to be utilised for
grazing shall be subdivided by fences into at least three paddocks,

          none of which shall exceed one half of the area within 2
years from the date of grant.


      (g) Yards and handling facilities to the satisfaction of the
Land Board shall be constructed within 2 years from the date

          of grant.


      (h) Conditions of improvements may at the discretion of the
Minister for Lands upon the recommendation of the

Land Board be modified in accordance with the detailed development

proposals of the applicant submitted in evidence to the

Land Board.


    Applicants are warned that applications must be lodged at or
posted so as to reach the Lands Department, Waigani, Papua

New Guinea before 3 p.m., Wednesday, 10th December, 1975. All
applications must be accompanied by the prescribed fee of

K2.00 for each lease required. Applications not conforming to these
requirements will be rejected as informal.


14th October, 1975.

display a ticket, label, placard. or notice -attached- to or,

shall within two years of date of grant, be fenced externally

           except in such parts of the boundaries as the presence of
natural features make this unnecessary, with a barbed wire fence

           of not less than four strands the topmost of which shall
be suspended not less than 1.1 metres above the ground and

           having posts not more than 4.5 metres apart, and strainer
posts at least every, 100 metres. The said fence to be kept

well strained, and in a stock-proof condition,

           of the total grazed area of the base, within 4 years from

Land Board shall be constructed within 2 years from the date

           of grant and maintained in serviceable condition for the
duration of the lease.

stocked as the following rate—

           and from the expiration of these periods the respective

THE Papua New Guinea National Gazette is published sectionally in
accordance with the following arrangements
  set out below:
Public Service Gazette
   Public Service issue contains notices concerning vacancies,
transfers and promotions within the Papua New
Guinea Public Service. These issues are published monthly at 11.30
a.m. on the first Thursday of each month.
General Gazette
  • General notices issue include the sittings of the House of
Assembly; Legislation (Acts assented to; Statutory
rules); Tenders etc. These issues are published weekly at 11.30 a.m.
on Thursday.
Special Gazette
   Special issues are made on urgent matters as required. Single
copies are available on the day of issue at the
Government Printing Office at 10 toea and are provided at no extra
charge with weekly issues.
Subscriptions
   Subscriptions are payable in advance. Rates are as follows:
   Within Papua New Guinea—including postage K15.00 per annum; K7.50
per half year; K3.75 per quarter;
   Australia—including postage K18.00 per annum; K9.00 per half
year; K4.50 per quarter;
   Overseas—including postage K55.00 per annum; K27.50 per half
year; K13.75 per quarter.
Notices
   "Notices for insertion" must be received at the Government

Printing Office, P.O. Box 3280, Port Moresby, be-
fore 11.30 a.m. on Friday preceding the day of publication excepting
the Public Service Board "Promotions and
Vacancies". Land Board advertisements must be lodged at 3 p.m. on
the afternoon preceding the normal closing
date.
   All notices, from whatever source, must have a covering
instruction setting out the publication details required.
The notice should be typewritten (double-spaced) on one side of the
paper only. Signatures in f articular and
proper names must be shown very plainly in the text. Copy, not
submitted in accordance with these instructions,

title: Papua New Guinea National Gazette G1-G10 (1975)

Papua New Guinea

National Gazette


                                      PUBLISHED BY AUTHORITY
                   (Registered at the General Post Office. Port
Moresby, for transmission by post as a Qualified Publication.)

No. 1                    PORT MORESBY, TUESDAY, 16th SEPTEMBER
1975

                    PROCLAMATION OF PAPUA NEW GUINEA'S INDEPENDENCE
     AT THE COMMENCEMENT OF THE SIXTEENTH DAY OF SEPTEMBER 1975, THE
GOVERNOR-
GENERAL, HIS EXCELLENCY SIR JOHN GUISE, K.B.E., AT PORT MORESBY,
PROCLAIMED THE
INDEPENDENCE AND FULL SOVEREIGNTY OF THE INDEPENDENT STATE OF PAPUA,
NEW
GUINEA, AND THE COMING INTO FORCE OF THE CONSTITUTION ADOPTED ON THE
FIF-
TEENTH DAY OF AUGUST, 1975 BY THE CONSIITUENT ASSEMBLY OF THE
ELECTED NATIONAL
                    REPRESENTATIVES OF THE PEOPLE OF PAPUA NEW
GUINEA.

                                               PUBLIC NOTICE
IT is hereby notified for public information that the Constitution
of the Independent State of Papua New Guinea
  shall come into effect on Independence Day, that is 16th
September,     975.
     Dated this fifth day of September, One thousand nine hundred
and     seventy-five.

B. HOLLOWAY,

Chairman of the Constituent Assembly.

                                  OPENING OF THE FIRST PARLIAMENT
IN accordance with Section 1 of the Organic Law on the. First
Meetings of the National Parliament, the first
  meeting of the First National Parliament will commence at 2 p.m.
this day at Parliament House, Port Moresby.
     The Parliament will be officially opened by His Royal Highness
the Prince Charles, Prince of Wales K.G.

                       FIRST GOVERNOR-GENERAL'S ASSUMPTION OF OFFICE
     On this day, by virtue of Section 268 of the Constitution, His
Excellency Sir John Guise K.B.E. assumed office

as the First Governor-General of the Independent State of Papua New
Guinea, and in accordance with Section 272
of the Constitution will take the oath of allegiance as prescribed
by Section 7 of the Constitution, and will make
the Declaration of Loyalty and the Declaration of Office as
prescribed by Section 6 and Schedule 3 of the Const-
itution, respectively in the following terms—
                                                Oath of Allegiance
         "I, JOHN GUISE, do swear that I will well and truly serve
and beat true allegiance to Her Majesty Queen
     Elizabeth II, Her heirs and successors according to law.
         SO HELP ME GOD!".


  1-16th-September, 1975   2             Papua New Guinea Gazette

             First Governor-General's Assumption of Office—continued
                      Declaration of Loyalty
    "I, JOHN GUISE, realizing fully the responsibilities to which I
am committing myself and the consequences
  of not living up to this Declaration and those responsibilities,
freely and willingly declare my loyalty to the
  Independent State of Papua New Guinea and its P,:ople and to the
Constitution of Papua New Guinea
  adopted by the Constitutent Assembly on 15th August, 1975, as
altered from time to time in accordance with
  its provisions, and promise that I will uphold the Constitution
and the laws of Papua New Guinea.".
                       Declaration of Office
    "I, JOHN GUISE, do promise and declare that I will well and
truly serve the Independent State of Papua
  New Guinea and its People in the office of Governor-General.".
                      FIRST CHIEF JUSTICE
  On this day, by virtue of Section 271 of the Constitution, the
HONOURABLE THOMAS SYDNEY FROST became
the first Chief Justice of the Independent State of Papua New
Guinea, and in accordance with Section 272 of the
Constitution, will duly make the Judicial Declaration prescribed by
Schedule 4 to the Constitution, in the follow-
ing terms--
    "I, THOMAS SYDNEY FROST, do promise and declare that I will well
and truly serve the Independent State
  of Papua New Guinea and its People in the office of Chief justice,
that I will in all things uphold the Const-
  itution and the laws of the Independent State of Papua New Guinea,
and I will do right to all manner of
  people in accordance therewith, without fear or favour, affection
or ill-will.
                     FIRST PRIME MINISTER
  On this day, by virtue of Section 270 of the Constitution, the
HONOURABLE MACHAEL SOMARE M.P. became
the First Prime Minister of the Independent State of Papua New
Guinea, and in accordance with Section 272 of the
Constitution will duly make the Declaration of Loyalty and the

Declaration of Office prescribed by Section 6 and
Schedule 3 of the Constitution respectively, in the following terms—
                       Declaration of Loyalty
    "I, MICHAEL THOMAS SOMARE, realizing fully the responsibilities
to which I am committing myself and
  the consequences of not living up to this Declaration and those
responsibilities, freely and willingly declare my
  loyalty to the Independent State of Papua New Guinea and its
People and to the Constitution of Papua New
  Guinea adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 15th August, 1975,
as altered from time to time in accordance
  with its provisions, and promise that I will uphold the
Constitution and the laws of Papua New Guinea.".
                        Declaration of Office
    "I, MICHAEL THOMAS SOMARE, do promise and declare that I will
well and truly serve the Independent
  State of Papua New Guinea and its People in the office of Prime
Minister.".
                        FIRST SPEAKER
  On this day, by virtue of Section 269 of the Constitution, the
HONOURABLE BARRY BLYTH HOLLOWAY C.B.E.
became the first Speaker of the National Parliament of the
Independent State of Papua New Guinea, and in
accordance with Section 272 of the Constitution will duly make the
Declaration of Loyalty and the. Declaration of
Office prescribed by Section 6 and Schedule 3 of the Constitution
respectively, in the following terms—
                       Declaration of Loyalty
    "I, BARRY BLYTH HOLLOWAY, realizing fully the responsibilities
to which I am committing myself and the
  consequences of not living up to this Declaration and those
responsibilities, freely and willingly declare my
  loyalty to the Independent State of Papua New Guinea and its
People and to the Constitution of Papua
  New. Guinea adopted by the Constitutent Assembly on 15th August,
1975, as altered from time to time in
  accordance with its provisions, and promise that I will uphold the
Constitution and the laws of Papua New
  Guinea.".
                        Declaration of Office
    "I, BARRY BLYTH HOLLOWAY, promise and declare that I will well
and truly serve the Independent State
  of Papua New Guinea and its People in the office of Speaker of the
National Parliament.".

                  FIRST DEPUTY PRIME MINISTER
  On this day, by virtue of Section 270 of the Constitution, the
HONOURABLE SIR MAORI KIKI K.B.E. M.P.
became the first Deputy Prime Minister of the Independent State of
Papua New Guinea and, in accordance with
Section 272 of the Constitution will duly make the Declaration of
Loyalty and the Declaration of Office prescribed by
Section 6 and Schedule 3 of the Constitution respectively, in the
following terms—

Declaration of Loyalty
    "I, ALBERT MAORI KIKI, realizing fully the responsibilities to
which I am committing myself and the
  consequences of not living up to this Declaration and those
responsibilities, freely and willingly declare my
  loyalty to the Independent State of Papua New Guinea and its
People and to the Constitution of Papua New
  Guinea adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 15th August, 1975,
as altered from time to time in accordance
  with its provisions, and promise that I will uphold the
Constitution and the laws of Papua New Guinea.".

became the first Deputy Chief Justice of the Independent State of
Papua New Guinea, and in accordance with
Section 272 of the Constitution, will duly make the Judicial
Declaration prescribed by Schedule 4 to the Const-
itution, in the following terms—
        "I, WILLIAM THOMAS PRENTICE, promise and declare that I will
well and truly serve the Independent
    State of Papua New Guinea and its People in the office of Deputy
Chief Justice, that I will in all things
    uphold the Constitution and the laws of the Independent State of
Papua New Guinea, and I will do right
    to all manner of people in accordance therewith, without fear or
favour, affection or ill-will.".
                                             FIRST JUDGES

following persons became the first Judges of
the National Court of the Independent State of Papua New Guinea, and
in accordance with Section 272 of the

         THE OMBUDSMAN COMMISSION—THE APPOINTMENT OF OMBUDSMEN
THE Papua New Guinea Constitution provides for the establishment of
the Ombudsman Commission immediately
   after Independence. The Commission will be an independent body
consisting of a Chief Ombudsman and
two Ombudsmen. They will be appointed by the Head of State on the
recommendation of the Ombudsman Ap-
pointments Committee. Members of the Commission are Constitutional
Office Holders under the Constitution.
   The Ombudsman Commission will have two main functions of
administering the Leadership Code and of hearing
complaints against the bureaucracy at the National and Provincial
Government levels.
   Applications are now called for from suitably qualified people
for appointment to the positions of Chief
Ombudsman and the Ombudsmen.
Chief Ombudsman
   Qualifications: The Chief Ombudsman needs to be a person of
integrity, independence of mind,
                   resolution and of a high standing in the
community. He needs to have qualities
                   which will enable him to enjoy the respect and
confidence of Ministers, Members of
                   Parliament and Provincial Assemblies and senior
public servants. Administrative
                   ability is essential. Desirably the appointee
should have a good knowledge of the
                   workings of the bureaucracy.
   Duties:         The Chief Ombudsman will have overall
responsibility for the functioning and
                   administration of the Ombudsman Commission; he
will allocate tasks to the other
                   Ombudsmen and will carry out enquiries as
appropriate.
   Benefits:       Salary will be appropriate for such a senior
appointment, but will not be less than
                   K8395 per annum. Other conditions will be not
less than those of a Judge who is a
                   citizen.


No. 8-3rd October, 1975              2                      National

Gazette


Ombudsmen
   Qualifications:The good general qualities required for the Chief
Ombudsman are also required of
                  both Ombudsmen. In addition, one is required to
have accountancy qualifications and
                  experience; the other is required to have
administrative or legal qualifications and
                  experience.
   Duties:        Under the direction of the Chief Ombudsman, the
Ombudsmen will assist in the work
                  of the Commission. The Ombudsman with accounting
qualifications and experience
                  can be expected to spend a fair amount of his time
on Leadership Code matters. The
                  other can be expected to be involved mainly in
matters relating to administrative acts
                  and decisions at national and provincial levels.
   Benefits:      Salary for these positions will be K7895 per
annum. Other conditions will be not less
                  than those of the Public Prosecutor.
Term of Appointment
   In the case of all three positions, the term of appointment will
be for three years with a possibility of re-
appointment.

Appointment of Public Servants
   If a Public Servant is appointed to one of these positions,
arrangements will be made for Public Service
rights to be preserved.

Address for Applications and Closing Date
   All applications should be addressed to:

          The Chairman,
          Ombudsman Appointments Committee,
          P.O. Box 2173,
          KONEDOBU.

                 MAXIMUM PRICES FOR BREAD—LAE
  MEKERE MORAUTA, Price Controller, by virtue of the powers
conferred by the Prices Regulation Act 1949, as
 amended to date, and all other powers me enabling, do hereby make
the following Order:—
                      PRICES ORDER No. 127
1. CITATION.
  This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 127.
2. COMMENCEMENT.
  This Order shall come into operation on the date of publication of
this Order in the Gazette.
3. REVOCATION.
  Prices Order No. 93 is hereby revoked.
4. DEFINITIONS.
  In this Order—
    "bread" means a product obtained by making a yeast leavened
dough prepared with flour and water with
      or without other ingredients;
    "foil-wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread that
such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery
      to the place at which the bread is sold by retail, in
aluminium or other foil, and that such bread was
      so enclosed when sold;

THE following persons have been duly nominated as candidates for the

POSITION OF DISTRICT COMMISSIONER

Applications are invited from suitably qualified persons both from
inside and outside the
Public Service of Papua New Guinea for two positions of District
Commissioner.

Appointment will be initially on a temporary basis with salary at
either the Class 11
($7,135) or Class 10 ($6,445-$6,675) salary levels, depending upon
experience and ability.
Successful applicants will be required to undergo a period of on-
the-job training before
advancement to District Commissioner, a level 1 appointment with an

annual salary of
$7,365.

Appointment as District Commissioner will be for three years and
will he subject to review
at the end of that term. An officer whose term of appointment is not
renewed will be placed
in a position with a salary classification not less than he held
before being selected for
training. For those persons engaged from outside the Public Service
the question of
continued employment will be subject to negotiation towards the end
of the period of
appointment.

Experience within the Department is oot essential. The Public
Service is seeking experierical
men with a high level of administrative and executive potential.
Applicants should have the
Public Service Higher Certificate or Form 6 or such other
educational qualifications as may
be acceptable to the Public Service Board.

Appointees after a short period of training will be appointed to a
District and will be
responsible to the Chief Minister for the co-ordination of
government policies and activities
in the district and the social, political and economic advancement
of the district.

                             MAXIMUM PRICES FOR BREAD—PORT MORESBY


il MEKERE MORAUTA, Price Controller, by virtue of the powers
conferred by the Prices Regulation Act 1949, as

   amended to date, and all other powers me enabling, do hereby make
the following Order:—


                                             PRICES ORDER No. 134


 1. CITATION.

This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 134.


 2. COMMENCEMENT.


     This Order shall come into operation on the date of publication
of this Order in the Gazette.


 3. REVOCATION.


     Prices Order No. 128 is hereby revoked.


 4. DEFINITIONS.


     In this Order—


       "bread" means a product obtained by baking a yeast leavened
dough prepared with flour and water with or

           without other ingredients;


       "ordinary bread" means bread made into loaves other than
starch-reduced bread, protein-increased bread or

           milk bread as defined in this Order or fancy bread;


       "milk bread" means bread which is made into loaves and which
contains no less than four parts per cent=

           by weight of non-fat milk solids calculated on the water-
free substance;


       "starch-reduced bread" or "protein increased bread" means
bread which is made into loaves and which con-

           tains not less than two and seven-tenths part per centum
by weight of nitrogen calculated on the water-

           free substance;


       "unwrapped" in relation to the sale of any bread means that
such bread is not wrapped as defined in this

           Order.

"wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread that
such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery to the

           place at which the bread is sold by retail, in waxed or
grease-proof paper, cellulose film, polythene or

           other similar wrapping and that such bread was so
enclosed when sold;


       "foil-wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread
that such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery

           to the place at which the bread is sold by retail, in
aluminium or other foil, and that such bread was


           so enclosed when sold;


 5. MEASUREMENT OF WEIGHT.


     Where, in this Order, the maximum price fixed is related to the
weight of bread, the weight is to be measured

when the bread is cold.


6. MAXIMUM PRICE.


     I fix and declare the maximum price at which bread included in
a category described in the first column of

the Schedule to this Order may be sold by retail in the City of Port
Moresby to be the price specified in the second

column of that Schedule opposite to the description of that
category.


 7. DISPLAY OF PRICES.


     A person or organisation engaged in selling bread by retail in
the City of Port Moresby, shall display in each

of their places of business, in prominent positions and in large
clear and legible figures, the types of bread loaves

covered by this Order and the prices at which such loaves may be

bought.

                           DESCRIPTION OF CURRENCY

AS required under Section 51(2) of the Central Banking Act 1973, the
denominations and other character-
  istics of Papua New Guinea legal tender currency issued by the
Bank of Papua New Guinea are as follows:—
1. BANKNOTES
     2 Kina — 140 MM x 70 MM
     5 Kina — 145 MM x 72.5 MM
    10 Kina — 150 MM x 75 MM
   The paper used is mould made panel banknote paper with a
substance of 83 grams per square metre into which
is incorporated a formal watermark of the Bank of Papua New Guinea's
logo and metallic security thread.
   All the banknotes feature the Papua New Guinea national crest on
the front. Each note is distinguished by
the different background tints surrounding the crest which depict
various traditional motifs.

Papua New Guinea Gazette


                                          Description of Currency-
continued


Two Kina K2


     (a) Front:-The background tints surrounding the national crest
on the front of the note comprise a tapa

cloth from the Central District, a Mount Hagen axe, a club from the
Huon Gulf area, a clay pot from the Sepik,

a shield from the Madang area, a marriage bed from Manus Island and
a shield from the Upper Sepik region.


     The designs surrounding the numerals represent local lineal art
patterns in modern style and do not interpret

any particular subject.


     (b) Back:-The back of this banknote features four main items: a
Mount Hagen axe, a kula arm band from

the Milne Bay District, engraved dogs teeth from the Bougainville
area and a clay pot from the Sepik. The back-

ground tints comprise patterns taken from a tapa cloth from the

Northern District, waist bands from the Gulf

District, a canoe from the Trobriand Islands, a shield from the
Sepik area, a canoe from the West Sepik area, a

Madang shield and clubs from the Huon Gulf region.


     The patterns used to surround the numerals in local artwork are
based on a bird design.


Five Kina K5


     (a) Front:-The background tints surrounding the national crest
on the front of this banknote comprise pat-

terns taken from the following items: a shield from the Gulf
District, a Sepik clay pot and Ramu River shields

from the Madang area. The patterns surrounding the numerals are
based on a slaughtered pig design.


     (b) Back:-The main designs on the back of the banknote comprise
four items of traditional Papua New

Guinea ''currencies": a Hombuli mask which is used for bridal
payments in the Sepik area, a kina shell from the

Highlands, a shell necklace from the Milne Bay area and a shell
necklace woven with seeds found in the New

Ireland District. The background tints for this design consist of a
Northern District tapa cloth, a Milne Bay shield

and tortoise shell bracelets from the Huon Gulf area.


     The patterns used to surround the numerals are based on a mask
design together with an illustration of a

bird.


Ten Kina K10


     (a) Front:-The background tints surrounding the national crest
on the front of this banknote include patterns

taken from the following items: a canoe from the Milne Bay District,
Sepik spears, a Madang shield, designs based

on patterns seen on a bow from the Highlands, a Sepik house post and
wood carvings from the New Ireland area.

The patterns surrounding the numerals are based on an illustration
of a bird.


     (b) Back:-The main design on the back of this banknote is
composed of the following items: a Tami bowl,

a bird of paradise skin, tambu shell money from the New Britain area
and boars tusks from the Highlands.


     The pattern surrounding the numeral is based on a
representation of a bird and a fish.


     The background tints for this banknote include patterns taken
from a Gulf shield, a ceremonial dance paddle

from Bougainville, a Sepik clay pot, a Gulf bark belt and marriage
bed posts from the Manus District.

                               MAXIMUM PRICES FOR BREAD—WEWAK


  MILTON FREDERICK ROBERTS, a Deputy Price Controller appointed
under the Prices Regulation Act 1949, as


  amended to date, hereby make the following Order under that Act:—


                                             PRICES ORDER No. 136


1. CITATION.

    This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 136.

2. COMMENCEMENT.


    This Order shall come into operation on the date of publication
of this Order in the Gazelle.


3. REVOCATION.


    Prices Order No. 95 is hereby revoked.


4. DEFINITIONS.

    In this Order—


       "bread" means a product obtained by baking a yeast leavened
dough prepared with flour and water with or


            without other ingredients;


       "ordinary bread" means bread made into loaves other than
starch-reduced bread, protein-increased bread or


            milk bread as defined in this Order or fancy bread;


       "milk bread" means bread which is made into loaves and which
contains no less than four parts per centum


            by weight of non-fat milk solids calculated on the
water-free substance;


       "starch-reduced bread" or "protein increased bread ' means
bread which is made into loaves and which con-


            tains not less than two and seven-tenths part per centum
by weight of nitrogen calculated on the water-

free substance;


       "unwrapped" in relation to the sale of any bread means that
such bread is not wrapped as defined in this


            Order.


       "wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread that
such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery to the


            place at which the bread is sold by retail, in waxed or
grease-proof paper, cellulose film, polythene or


            other similar wrapping and that such bread was so
enclosed when sold;


       "foil-wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread
that such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery


            to the place at which the bread is sold by retail, in
aluminium or other foil, and that such bread was


            so enclosed when sold;


5. MEASUREMENT OF WEIGHT.


    Where, in this Order, the maximum price fixed is related to the
weight of bread, the weight is to be measured


when the bread is cold.


6. MAXIMUM PRICE.


    I fix and declare the maximum price at which bread included in a
category described in the first column of

the Schedule to this Order may be sold by retail in the town of
Wewak to he the price specified in the second column

of that Schedule opposite to the description of that category.


7. DISPLAY OF PRICES.


    A person or organisation engaged in selling bread by retail in
the Town of Wewak, shall display in each


of their places of business, in prominent positions and in large
clear and legible figures, the types of bread loaves


covered by this Order and the prices at which such loaves may be
bought.

                                      PRICES ORDER No. 154

                                                being
APRICES ORDER relating to the maximum wholesale and retail price for

                                               BREAD

                                    LAE AND PORT MORESBY

   Made by the price Controller under the provisions of the Prices
Regulation Act 1949, as amended to date, to
   come into operation on the date of publication in the National
Gazette.

 1. CITATION.
   This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 154.

2. REVOCATION.

   Prices Order No. 134 and Prices Order No. 135 are hereby revoked.

3. DEFINITIONS.
   In this Order—

     "bread" means a product obtained by baking a yeast leavened
dough prepared with flour and water with or
          without other ingredients;

     "ordinary bread" means bread made into loaves other than
starch-reduced bread, protein-increased bread or
          milk bread as defined in this Order or fancy bread;

     "milk bread" means bread which is made into loaves and which
contains no less than four parts per centum
          by weight of non-fat milk solids calculated on the water-
free substance;
     "starch-reduced bread" or "protein increased bread" means bread
which is made into loaves and which
          contains not less than two and seven-tenths parts per
centum by weight of nitrogen calculated on the
          water-free substance;

     "unwrapped" in relation to the sale of any bread means that
such bread is not wrapped as defined in this
          Order;

     "wrapped" means in relation    to the sale of any bread that such
bread is fully enclosed prior to    delivery to
           the place at which the   bread is sold by retail, in waxed
or grease-proof paper, cellulose    film, polythene or
           other similar wrapping   and that such bread was so enclosed
when sold;


 National Gazette                                                5
No. 21-20th November, 1975


                                              Prices Order No. 154--
continued

        "foil-wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread
that such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery

             to the place at which the bread is sold by retail, in
aluminium or other foil, and that such bread was

             so enclosed when sold.

4. MEASUREMENT OF WEIGHT.

     Where, in this Order, the maximum price fixed is related to the
weight of bread, the weight is to be measured

 when the bread is cold.

     5. MAXIMUM PRICE.

     The maximum price at which bread included in a category
described in the first column of the Schedule to this

 Order may be sold by wholesale and retail in the cities of Lae and
Port Moresby is the price specified in the second

column of that Schedule opposite to the description of that
category.

     6. DISPLAY OF PRICES.

     A person or organisation engaged in selling bread by retail in
the Cities of Lae and Port Moresby, shall dis-

play in each of their places of business, in prominent positions and
in large clear and legible figures, the types of

bread loaves covered by this Order and the prices at which such
loaves may be bought.

                                                   PRICES ORDER No. 155

                                                                    being
A PRICES ORDER relating to the maximum retail price for

                               PETROL, DISTILLATE AND LIGHTING
KEROSENE

     Made by the Deputy Price Controller under the provisions of the
Prices Regulation Aet-1949, as amended to
     date, to come into operation on the date of publication in the
National Gazette.
1. CITATION.

This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 155.
2. REVOCATION.
     The Prices Orders specified in Schedule 2 of this Order are
revoked.
3. DEFINITIONS.
     In this Order—
         "petrol" includes any substance normally sold as petrol
whether or not containing additives of any kind;
         "distillate" includes any substance normally sold as
automotive distillate whether or not containing additives
              of any kind;
         "kerosene" includes any substance normally sold as kerosene
being a medium refined petroleum product as
              used for lighting and cooking in home appliances,
whether or not containing additives of any kind;
         "wholesaler" in relation to petrol, distillate or lighting
kerosene means a person or a firm who sells petrol,
              distillate or lighting kerosene for the purpose of
resale and not for the purpose of use;
         "supplier" in relation to petrol, distillate or lighting
kerosene, means a person or a firm who sells petrol,
              distillate or lighting kerosene for the purpose of use;
         "retail" means for the purpose of consumption or use.

4. MAXIMUM PRICE.

      (i) Subject to Subclause (ii) of this clause, where petrol,
distillate or kerosene is supplied-

        (a) at a locality specified in the first column of Schedule
I to this Order; or

        (b) at some other place at which the petrol, distillate or
lighting kerosene is transported from any such
             locality by or on behalf of a wholesaler, or supplier;

the maximum price per gallon at which the petrol, distillate or
kerosene may be supplied is the sum of-

        (c) the maximum retail selling price specified in the
Second, Third or Fourth Column as the case may be, of
             Schedule I in relation to the locality concerned; and

        (d) the amount (if any) charged for the transport referred
to in paragraph (b) of this subclause.

(ii) Where the maximum price of any quantity of petrol,
distillate or kerosene supplied at any one time, cal-
culated in accordance with Subclause (i) of this clause is an amount
involving a fraction of a toea, the supplier
may charge to the next whole toea.

5. SUPPLY TO GOVERNMENT ETC.

     Nothing in this Order applies to or relates to the supply of
petrol, distillate or kerosene to the Government or
instrumentality or authority of the Government.

6. DISPLAY OF PRICES.

     A person or an organisation engaged in selling petrol,
distillate or lighting kerosene by retail shall display in
each of the places of business in prominent positions and in large
clear and legible figures the maximum prices
at which such petrol, distillate and kerosene may be bought.

                       Liquor (Licensing) Act 1963

                   PROHIBITION OF SUPPLY OF LIQUOR
     JOHN GUISE, G.C.M.G., Governor-General, by virtue of the powers
conferred by Section 124 of the Liquor
   9 (Licensing) Act 1963 and all other powers me enabling, acting
with, and in accordance with, the advice of
   the National Executive Council, hereby—
      (a) prohibit the supply of liquor under any licence or permit
throughout Papua New Guinea-
          (i) on a day which is a public holiday; and
          (ii) on a Saturday and Sunday when the preceding Friday or
the following Monday is a public
            holiday; and
      (b) notwithstanding anything in this notice each holder of a
publican's licence, limited hotel licence or
        residential club licence may supply liquor for consumption
on licensed premises at any time to lodgers.
     In this notice "public holiday" means a day which is a public
holiday under the Public Holidays Act 1953.

Dated this sixteenth day of December, One thousand nine hundred
and seventy-five.

     MILTON FREDERICK ROBERTS, a Deputy Price Controller, by virtue
of the powers conferred by the Prices Reg-
    ' elation Act 1949, as amended to date, and all other powers me
enabling, do hereby make the following Order
   under that Act:—
                          PRICES ORDER No. 138
   1. CITATION.
      This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 138.
   2. COMMENCEMENT.
      This Order shall come into operation on the date of
publication of this Order in the Gazette.
   3. REVOCATION.
      The Prices Orders specified in Schedule 2 of this Order are
revoked.
   4. DEFINITIONS.
      In this Order—
       "petrol", includes any substance normally sold a petrol
whether or not containing additives of any kind;
       "distillate" includes any substance normally sold a
automotive distillate whether or not containing additives
         of any kind;
       "kerosene" includes any substance normally sold a kerosene,
being a medium refined petroleum product as
         used for lighting and cooking in home appliances, whether
or not containing additives of any kind;
       "wholesaler" in relation to petrol, distillate or kerosene
means a person or a firm who sells petrol, dis-
         tillate or kerosene for the purpose of resale and not for
the purpose of use;
       "supplier" in relation to petrol, distillate or kerosene,
means a person or a firm who sells petrol, distillate
         or kerosene for the purpose of use;
       "retail" means for the purpose of consumption or use.
   5. MAXIMUM PRICE.

(i) Subject to Subclause (ii) of this clause, where petrol,
distillate or kerosene is supplied—
       (a) at a locality specified in the first column of Schedule 1
to this Order; or
       (b) at some other place to which the petrol, distillate or
kerosene is transported from any such locality by
         or on behalf of a wholesaler or the supplier;
   the maximum price per gallon at which the petrol, distillate or
kerosene may be supplied is the sum of—
       (c) the maximum retail selling price specified in the Second,
Third or Fourth Column as the case may be, of
         Schedule 1 in relation to the locality concerned; and
       (d) the amount (if any) charged for the transport referred to
in paragraph (b) of this subclause.

TENDERS and/or applications, as applicable, are invited for the
right to a lease or leases over the land or lands as described
in the following advertisements on the terms and conditions as set
out and subject to the provisions of the Land Act 1962 (as
amended)
The attention of tenderer' and applicants is directed towards the
following:-
Tenders.-The upset price where shown below is the assessed
unimproved value of the land, and is the minimum amount
acceptable as a tender. Tenders may be for any amount in
excess of the upset price, but the successful tenderer will only
be required to pay the difference between the upset price and
the amount of the tender.

Fees.-All tenders and applications must be accompanied
by an application fee of One Kina (K1) for each, portion
or allotment required. Following the grant of a lease an
additional fee for the preparation of lease document, the
amount of tender less the upset price where applicable and,
if surveyed, the prescribed survey fee shall be payable within
two (2) months from the date of grant.
Preference.-Tenderers and applicants are advised to indicate
preferences if there are more than one allotment or portion

being advertised in any particular advertisement, but only one
registration of application fee need be lodged if only one
allotment or portion is required. If more than one allotment or
portion is required, an additional fee for each such portion or
allotment must be lodged.
Tenderers and Applicants.-Tendcrers and applicants must
state full name, occupation and postal address. If more than
one person is tendering or applying, it must be stated whether
joint tenancy or tenancy-in-common is required. If a company,
the full registered name and address of the company and that
of its representative must be stated, A business name cannot
hold land.
Improvements.-Expected development in respect of agricul-
tural leases is indicated in the respective advertisements; how-
ever, full proposals of proposed development shall be submitted
by tenderers or applicants seeking other types of leases or
larger agricultural leases unless development is specified in
detail in any particular advertisement. Where applicable devel-
opment shall comply with the requirements of the Town Plan-
ning Act and the Building Regulations.
Term of Lease.-Unless otherwise indicated each lease shall
be for a term of ninety-nine (99) years.
General condition' pertaining to Business Leases.-Provided
all other factors are equal, preference may be given to indig-
enous proposals, or proposals which contain a significant pro-
portion of indigenous equity. In the event that a lease is
recommended because of a proposal to include a significant
portion of indigenous equity, the lease shall contain a clause
requiring specific performance of that proposal within a time
specified. In all cases where a lease is granted to non-Papua
New Guineans or companies or associations not containing a
significant amount of the indigenous equity, the lease may
contain a clause requiring the lessee to achieve a specific level

Improvements.—Section 57 of the Land Act 1962-74, provides that
an Agricultural Lease shall contain conditions prescribing

the minimum improvements to be carried out by the Lessee. Conditions
applicable to the leases described above are as follows:-


      1. Of the land suitable for cultivation the following
proportions shall be planted in a good and husbandlike manner with

           a crop or crops of economic value which shall be
harvested regularly in accordance with sound commercial practice:


            (a) One-tenth in the first period of 2 years of the
term;


            (b) One-fifth in the first period of 5 years of the
term;


            and during the remainder of the term, one-fifth of the
land so suitable shall be kept so planted.


      2. That portion of the lease which is to be utilised for
grazing shall be stocked with a minimum of 1 head of great cattle

           per 3 hectares within 5 years from date of grant, and
shall be kept so stocked to that minimum for the remainder of the

           term.


      3. That portion of the lease which is to be utilised for
grazing shall within 3 years from the date of grant be fenced exter-

           nally, except in such parts of the boundaries as the
presence of natural features make this unnecessary with a barbed

           wire fence of not less than 4 strands having posts not
more than 4.5 metres (15 feet) apart, and strainer posts at

           least every 100 metres (5 chains), the said fence to be
kept well strained and in stock-proof condition.

4. That portion of the Lease which is to be utilised for
grazing shall be subdivided by fencing into at least 3 paddocks,

           within 3 years from the date of grant. Any one paddock
shall not exceed more than half of the area used for grazing.


      5. Yards and handling facilities to the satisfaction of the
Land Board shall be constructed within 3 years of the date of

             grant.


      6. Condition of improvements may, at the discretion of the
Minister for Lands upon the recommendation of the Land

           Board, be modified in accordance with the detailed

                VACANCY—CENTRAL PLANNING OFFICE
               ASSOCIATE DIRECTOR—POSITION No. C12(T)
APPLICATIONS are invited from suitably qualified persons for
selection as the Associate Director of the Central
  Planning Office.
  The salary payable will be negotiable but will be not less than
K7,365 per annum (Level 1).
  The successful applicant will undertake a programm of training
with a view to early promotion to the position
of Director of the Central Planning Office, subject to satisfactory
performance. He will be given the earliest possible
opportunity to take full responsibility for the duties of the
position.
  The duties of the Director include:
   —Direct, control, plan and co-ordinate the activities of the
Central Planning Office.
   —Advise the National Planning Committee of Cabinet and individual
Ministers on policy matters.
   —Propose integrated policies to achieve the Government's
objectives and incorporate these policies into a
      National Improvement Programme.
   —Ensure transmission of approved policy to departments and areas.
   —Oversee implementation, report on progress and recommend action.
   —Hold statutory appointments and act as a member of Councils,
Boards and Committees related to the func-
      tions of the Office.
, 'Applicants should have a good educational background desirably
including relevant tertiary qualifications;
brillOsing ability; ability to manage technical experts and
communicate to decision makers.

    Improvements:—Section 57 of the Land Act 1962-74 provides that
an Agricultural Lease shall contain conditions prescribing
the minimum improvements to be carried out by the lessee. Conditions
applicable to the lease above are as follows:

       (a) Of the land suitable for cultivation the following

proportions shall be planted in a good and husbandlike manner with
           a crop or pasture species of economic value which shall
be harvested regularly in accordance with sound commercial
           practice-

            One-fifth in the first period of 5 years of the term;
            Three-fifths in the first period of 10 years of the
term;
            Four-fifths in the first period of 15 years of the term;

           and during the remainder of the term four-fifths of the
land so suitable shall be kept so planted.

       (b) That portion of the lease to be utilised for grazing
shall be stocked with a minimum of 1 head of great cattle per 5
           hectares within 3 years from the date of grant and shall
be kept so stocked to that minimum for the remainder of the
           term.
       (c) That portion of the lease which shall be utilised for
grazing shall, from within 2 years of the date of grant, be fenced
           externally except in such parts where the natural
features make this unnecessary, with a barbed-wire fence of not less
           than 4 strands, the topmost of which shall be not less
than 1 metre above the ground and having posts not more
           than 4.5 metres apart and strainer posts at least every
100 metres, the said fence to be kept well-strained and in a stock-
           proof condition.
       (d) The area which is to be utilised for grazing shall within
3 years from the date of grant be subdivided by fences into a
           minimum of 4 paddocks none of which shall enclose more
than half of the total area to be used for grazing, and for
           the duration of the lease the said area shall be kept so
subdivided and the said fence maintained in stock-proof con-
           dition.

       (e) Yards and handling facilities to the satisfaction of the
Land Board shall be constructed within 2 years from the date of
           grant.
       (f) Provided always that if at the end of the first 2 years
of the lease it appears that reasonable efforts are not being made
           to fulfil the improvement conditions, the Minister for
Lands may, by notice in the Gazette, and in accordance with
           the provisions of the Land Act 1962-74, forfeit the
lease.

                             MAXIMUM PRICES FOR BREAD—RABAUL

21 MILTON FREDERICK ROBERTS, a Deputy Price Controller appointed
under the Prices Regulation Act 1949, as

  amended to date, hereby make the following Order under that Act:—


                                           PRICES ORDER No. 141


1. CITATION.


       This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 141.

2. COMMENCEMENT.

    This Order shall come into operation on the date of publication
of this Order in the Gazette,


3. REVOCATION.

    Prices Order No. 94 is hereby revoked.


4. DEFINITIONS.

    In this Order—


     "bread" means a product obtained by baking a yeast leavened
dough prepared with flour and water with

         or without other ingredients;


     "ordinary bread" means bread made into loaves other than
starch-reduced bread, protein-increased bread or

         milk bread as defined in this Order or fancy bread;


     "milk bread" means bread which is made into loaves and which
contains no less than four parts per centurn

         by weight of non-fat milk solids calculated on the water-
free substance;


     "starch-reduced bread" or "protein increased bread" means bread
which is made into loaves and which

         contains not less than two and seven-tenths part per centum
by weight of nitrogen calculated on the

         water-free substance;


     "unwrapped" in relation to the sale of any bread means that
such bread is not wrapped as defined in

         this Order.


     "wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread that such
bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery to

the place at which the bread is sold by retail, in waxed or
grease-proof paper, cellulose film, poly-

         thene or other similar wrapping and that such bread was so
enclosed when sold;


     "foil-wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread that
such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery

         to the place at which the bread is sold by retail, in
aluminium or other foil, and that such bread was

            so enclosed when sold.

5. MEASUREMENT OF WEIGHT.

    Where, in this Order, the maximum price fixed is related to the
weight of bread, the weight is to be

measured when the bread is cold.


6. MAXIMUM PRICE.

    I fix and declare the maximum price at which bread included in a
category described in the first column

of the Schedule to this Order may be sold by wholesale and retail in
the town of Rabaul to be the price specified in

the second column of that Schedule opposite to the description of
that category.


7. DISPLAY OF PRICES.

    A person or organisation engaged in selling bread by retail in
the Town of Rabaul, shall display in each of

their places of business, in prominent positions and in large clear
and legible figures, the types of bread loaves

covered by this Order and the prices at which such loaves may be
bought.

                          MAXIMUM PRICES FOR PETROL, DISTILLATE AND
LIGHTING KEROSENE
.1 MILTON FREDERICK ROBERTS, a Deputy Price Controller, by virtue of
the powers conferred by the Prices Regu-
      lation Act 1949, as amended to date, and all other powers me
enabling do hereby make the following Order
under that Act:—

PRICES ORDER No. 122
1. CITATION.
         This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 122.
2. COMMENCEMENT.
         This Order shall come into operation on the date of
publication of this Order in the Gazette.
3. REVOCATION.
         The Prices Orders specified in Schedule 2 of this Order are
revoked.
4. DEFINITIONS.
         In this Order—

"petrol" includes any substance normally sold as petrol whether or
not containing additives of any kind;
"distillate" includes any substance normally sold as automotive
distillate whether or not containing additives of
any kind;
"kerosene" includes any substance normally sold as kerosene, being a
medium refined petroleum product as
used for lighting and cooking in home appliances, whether or not
containing additives of any kind;
"wholesaler" in relation to petrol, distillate or kerosene means a
person or a firm who sells petrol, distillate
or kerosene for the purpose of resale and not for the purpose of
use;
"supplier" in relation to petrol, distillate or kerosene, means a
person or a firm who sells petrol, distillate or
kerosene for the purpose of use;
"retail" means for the purpose of consumption or, use.
5. MAXIMUM PRICE.
(i) Support to Subclause (ii) of this clause, where petrol,
distillate or kerosene is supplied -
(a) at a locality specified in, the first column of Schedule 1 to
this Order; or
(b) at some other place to which the petrol, distillate or kerosene
is transported from any such locality by or
on behalf of a wholesaler or the supplier;
the maximum price per gallon at which the petrol, distillate or
kerosene may be supplied is the sum of-
(c) the maximum retail selling price specified in the second, third
or fourth column as the case may be, of
Schedule 1 in relation to the locality concerned; and
(d) the amount (if any) charged for the transport referred to in
paragraph (b) of this subclause.
(ii) Where the maximum price of any quantity of petrol, distillate
or kerosene supplied at any one time, cal-
culated in accordance with Subclause (i) of this clause is an amount
involving a fraction of a cent, the supplier
may charge to the next whole cent.
6. SUPPLY TO GOVERNMENT ETC.
Nothing in this Order applies to or in relation to the supply of
petrol, distillate or kerosene to the Govern-
ment, Australia or a Statutory Authority of the Government or
Australia.
7. NOTICES FIXING MAXIMUM PRICES.
Notwithstanding the preceding provisions of this Order, the
Controller may, by notice in writing to any person
or body or association of persons, fix the maximum price at which
petrol, distillate or kerosene may be sold, and
thereupon that maximum price is the price for the purpose of the

    MILTON FREDIIIUCK ROBERTS, a Deputy Price Controller appointed
under the Prices Regulation Act 1949, as
   amended to date, hereby make the following Order under that Act:-

                                          PRICES ORDER No. 124
1. CITATION.
     This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 124.

2. COMMENCEMENT.

     This Order shall come into operation on the date of publication
of this Order in the Gazelle.

3. REVOCATION.
     Prices Order No. 92 is hereby revoked.

4. DEFINITIONS.
     In this Order-

       "cigarettes" means cigarettes which are manufactured in Papua
New Guinea from imported or locally grown
            tobacco leaf.

       "retail" means for the purpose of consumption or use.

5. MAXIMUM PRICE.

     (a) The maximum price per packet at which cigarettes may be
sold by retail at any of the locations specified

in Schedule 1 is the amount specified in the Second Column of
Schedule 2 in relation to the brand and pack spe-
cified opposite in the First Column of Schedule 2.

       (b) The maximum price per packet at which cigarettes may be
sold by retail at locations other than those

 specified in Schedule 1 is the amount specified in the Third Column
of Schedule 2 in relation to the brand and
 pack specified opposite in the First Column of Schedule 2.

    6. DISPLAY OF PRICES.

       A person or organisation who has in his custody or under his
control any of the cigarettes to which this Order

 applies for sale by retail, or who, offers, exhibits or exposes any
of those cigarettes for sale by retail, shall display
 a ticket, label, placard or notice attached to or exhibited or
displayed with the cigarettes setting forth in a prominent

 position in dear and legible figures easily discernible to any
person inspecting such cigarettes, the price at which the
 cigarettes concerned may be bought.

    7. MAXIMUM RETAIL PRICE OF CIGARETTES IN CERTAIN AREAS.

       Notwithstanding anything in this Order, where a notice in
writing is given by the Controller to a supplier of
 cigarettes fixing the maximum price at which cigarettes may be
supplied by him in any locality, being a price not
 less than fixed by Clause 4 of this Order, the maximum price at
which cigarettes may be so supplied is the price
 fixed in that Notice.

Improvements:—Section 57 of the Land Act 1962-1974 provides that
an Agricultural Lease shall contain conditions prescrib•

ing the minimum improvements to be carried out by the lessee.
Conditions applicable to the leases described above are as follows:—


     Of the land suitable for cultivation the following proportions
shall be planted in a good and husbandlike manner with a

        crop or crops of economic value which shall be harvested
regularly in accordance with sound commercial practice:-


        One-fifth in the first period of 5 years of the term;


        Two-fifths in the first period of 10 years of the term;


        Three-fifths in the first period of 15 years of the term;


        Four-fifths in the first period of 20 years of the term;


        and during the remainder of the term four-fifths of the land
so suitable shall be kept so planted. Provided always that

        if at the end of the first two years of the term of the
lease the lessee has not cleared and prepared for planting or

        or planted a minimum area of one-tenth of the land so suited
the Minister for Lands may if he thinks fit, by notice in

        the Gazette and in accordance with the provisions of the
Land Act 1962-1974 forfeit the lease.


   Eligibility:—Applications will be accepted from Papua New
Guineans only.


   Residence Condition:—The lessee or his agent shall take up
residency or occupancy of his block within 6 months from the

date of grant.


   Applicants are warned that applications must be lodged at or
posted so as to reach the Lands Department, Waigani, Papua

New Guinea before 3 p.m., 23rd April, 1975. Applications must be
accompanied by the prescribed fee of $2.00 for each lease re-

quired. Applications not conforming to these requirements will be
rejected as informal.

Suitable for a crocodile farm

                    Kikori


   1. Conditions applicable to the lease described above are as
follows:—


     Of the land suitable for cultivation the following proportions
shall be planted in a good and husbandlike manner with a

crop or crops of economic value which shall be harvested
regularly in accordance with sound commercial practice:-


        One-tenth in the first period of 5 years of the term;


        One-fifth in the first period of 10 years of the term;


        and during the remainder of the term one-fifth of the land
so suited shall be kept so planted.


   2. Residence condition:—The lessee or his agent shall take up
residency or occupancy of his block within 6 months from the

date of grant.


   3. Housing, fencing and ancillary works and equipment for fencing
crocodiles to the value of $2,000 to he erected within 1

year of date of grant and for the remainder of the term of the lease
improvements to this value shall be maintained in serviceable

condition.


   4. Crocodiles shall only be kept on the lease within a secure
enclosure. Such enclosure shall be a wall or fence erected:


     (a) to a minimum height of 1.22 metres (4 feet) above the
surface of the ground within the enclosure;


     (b) if a material or design permitting the animals assistance
to climb, a horizontal component shall be added to the top of

        the fence and shall extend not less than 0.45 metres into
the pen and shall be of a durable material and design;


     (c) The fence shall be of a design to the satisfaction of the
Land Board and shall contain such reinforcement to a depth

        beneath the fence of not less than 0.3 metre (1 foot)
(greater where the soil is of a type to offer average or less

        resistance to digging by crocodiles).

4. At all times during the term of the lease the aforementioned
fences shall be maintained in a sound and stock-proof condi-

tion. No crocodiles greater than 0.510 metre by belly width shall be
kept on the lease.


   5. The lessee shall not discharge, suffer or permit to be
discharged into the Kikori River or its tributaries any offal, waste
or

decayed food but will dispose of same by either complete
incineration or burying to a depth not less than 0.5 metres.


   6. Waste water and drainage from the pens shall not be discharged
directly into the Kikori River.


   7. The lessee shall take all care to warn against and prevent
entry of the public into the area used for keeping crocodiles.


   8. No trade, business or activity shall he carried out on the
lease which is, in itself or in a manner in which it is carried out,

contrary to any law, act, regulation or by-law which may he in force
on the lease or part thereof.


   9. Provided always that if at the end of the first 2 years of the
term the lessee has not cleared and prepared for planting or

planted a minimum area of one-tenth of the land so suited the Land
Board may recommend the Minister for Lands to forfeit the

lease and thereupon the Minister for Lands may if be thinks fit by
notice in the Gazette and in accordance with the provisions of

the Land Act 1962-1974 forfeit the lease accordingly.


   10. Applicants are warned that applications must be lodged at or
posted so as to reach the Lands Department, Waigani, Papua

New Guinea before 3 p.m., Wednesday, 9th April, 1975. All
applications must be accompanied by the prescribed fee of $2.00 for

each lease required. Applications not conforming to these
requirements will be rejected as informal.

that an Agricultural Lease shall contain conditions pre-

scribing the minimum improvements to be carried out by the lessee.
Conditions applicable to the leases described above are as

follows:-


        Of the land suitable for cultivation the following planting
shall be carried out in a good and husbandlike manner and

             shall he harvested regularly in accordance with sound
commercial practice.


        Four hundred and eighty oil palms at a spacing of 32 feet in
a triangular pattern in the first year of the term at the rate of-


              (i) Two hundred and forty oil palms (about 2 ha.) in
the first 6 months of the first year of the term;

              (ii) Two hundred and forty oil palms in the second 6
months of the first year of the term; and


             during the remainder of the term 4 hectares of the land
so suitable shall be kept so planted, and of the total area suit-

             able for cultivation, four-fifths shall he cleared and
under cultivation from within 10 years from the date of grant, and

             during the remainder of the term this portion of the
land shall be kept cleared and cultivated.


      Residence condition:-Applicants are advised that the following
conditions will apply to each lease:-


        The lessee shall within 2 months of the date of grant, or
such longer period not exceeding 6 months, as may appear

             suitable to the Director of Lands, Surveys and Mines
take up residence on his lease and continue in residence for a

             minimum period of 7 years.


      The Land Board is recommended to release only one block to any
one applicant.


      Applicants are warned that applications must be lodged at or

posted so as to reach the Lands Department, Waigani, Papua

New Guinea before 3 p.m., Friday, 6th June, 1975. All applications
must be accompanied by the prescribed fee of Two Dollars

for each lease.


      Applications not conforming to these requirements will he
rejected as informal.


      Applicants are further warned that the onus is on them to
provide a sufficient address for postage of notices and to advise

the Director of Lands in writing of any change of address. An
otherwise successful applicant who fails in this regard could have

his rights to a lease extinguished under Section 38 of the Land Act
1962-74.


      Formal applications lodged for these blocks in response to
Notice No. 138/74 will be considered along with applications

in response to this advertisement.

PRICES ORDER No. 122
1. CITATION.
         This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 122.
2. COMMENCEMENT.
         This Order shall come into operation on the date of
publication of this Order in the Gazette.
3. REVOCATION.
         The Prices Orders specified in Schedule 2 of this Order are
revoked.
4. DEFINITIONS.
         In this Order—

"petrol" includes any substance normally sold as petrol whether or
not containing additives of any kind;
"distillate" includes any substance normally sold as automotive
distillate whether or not containing additives of
any kind;
"kerosene" includes any substance normally sold as kerosene, being a
medium refined petroleum product as
used for lighting and cooking in home appliances, whether or not
containing additives of any kind;
"wholesaler" in relation to petrol, distillate or kerosene means a
person or a firm who sells petrol, distillate
or kerosene for the purpose of resale and not for the purpose of
use;
"supplier" in relation to petrol, distillate or kerosene, means a
person or a firm who sells petrol, distillate or
kerosene for the purpose of use;
"retail" means for the purpose of consumption or, use.
5. MAXIMUM PRICE.
(i) Support to Subclause (ii) of this clause, where petrol,
distillate or kerosene is supplied -
(a) at a locality specified in, the first column of Schedule 1 to
this Order; or
(b) at some other place to which the petrol, distillate or kerosene
is transported from any such locality by or
on behalf of a wholesaler or the supplier;
the maximum price per gallon at which the petrol, distillate or
kerosene may be supplied is the sum of-
(c) the maximum retail selling price specified in the second, third
or fourth column as the case may be, of
Schedule 1 in relation to the locality concerned; and
(d) the amount (if any) charged for the transport referred to in
paragraph (b) of this subclause.
(ii) Where the maximum price of any quantity of petrol, distillate
or kerosene supplied at any one time, cal-
culated in accordance with Subclause (i) of this clause is an amount
involving a fraction of a cent, the supplier
may charge to the next whole cent.
6. SUPPLY TO GOVERNMENT ETC.
Nothing in this Order applies to or in relation to the supply of
petrol, distillate or kerosene to the Govern-
ment, Australia or a Statutory Authority of the Government or
Australia.
7. NOTICES FIXING MAXIMUM PRICES.

broadcast techniques. (Appointment depending upon experience,
qualif-

-

with

                                        MAXIMUM PRICES FOR CIGARETTES

    MILTON FREDIIIUCK ROBERTS, a Deputy Price Controller appointed
under the Prices Regulation Act 1949, as
   amended to date, hereby make the following Order under that Act:-

                                          PRICES ORDER No. 124
1. CITATION.
     This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 124.

2. COMMENCEMENT.

     This Order shall come into operation on the date of publication
of this Order in the Gazelle.

3. REVOCATION.
     Prices Order No. 92 is hereby revoked.

4. DEFINITIONS.
     In this Order-

       "cigarettes" means cigarettes which are manufactured in Papua
New Guinea from imported or locally grown
            tobacco leaf.

       "retail" means for the purpose of consumption or use.

5. MAXIMUM PRICE.

     (a) The maximum price per packet at which cigarettes may be
sold by retail at any of the locations specified

in Schedule 1 is the amount specified in the Second Column of
Schedule 2 in relation to the brand and pack spe-
cified opposite in the First Column of Schedule 2.

Cigarettes—continued

       (b) The maximum price per packet at which cigarettes may be
sold by retail at locations other than those

 specified in Schedule 1 is the amount specified in the Third Column
of Schedule 2 in relation to the brand and
 pack specified opposite in the First Column of Schedule 2.

    6. DISPLAY OF PRICES.

       A person or organisation who has in his custody or under his
control any of the cigarettes to which this Order

 applies for sale by retail, or who, offers, exhibits or exposes any
of those cigarettes for sale by retail, shall display
 a ticket, label, placard or notice attached to or exhibited or
displayed with the cigarettes setting forth in a prominent

 position in dear and legible figures easily discernible to any
person inspecting such cigarettes, the price at which the
 cigarettes concerned may be bought.

    7. MAXIMUM RETAIL PRICE OF CIGARETTES IN CERTAIN AREAS.

       Notwithstanding anything in this Order, where a notice in
writing is given by the Controller to a supplier of
 cigarettes fixing the maximum price at which cigarettes may be
supplied by him in any locality, being a price not
 less than fixed by Clause 4 of this Order, the maximum price at
which cigarettes may be so supplied is the price
 fixed in that Notice.

PRICES ORDER No. 142
being
A PRICES ORDER relating to the maximum retail price for aviation
gasoline.

MADE by the Price Controller under the provisions of the Prices
Regulation Act 1949, as amended to date, to come
into operation on the date of publication in the Government Gazette.
1. DEFINITIONS.
In this Order—
"aviation gasoline" includes any substance normally sold as aviation
gasoline whether or not containing
additives of any kind;
"supplier" in relation to aviation gasoline, means a person or a
firm who sells aviation gasoline for the
purpose of consumption or use;
"retail" means for the purpose of consumption or use.
2. MAXIMUM RETAIL PRICE.
(i) Where aviation gasoline is supplied at a locality specified in
Column I of Schedule I, the maximum price
per gallon at which the aviation gasoline may be supplied is the
maximum retail selling price specified in Column
2 of that Schedule in relation to the locality concerned; and
(ii) Where the maximum price of any quantity of aviation gasoline,
supplied at any one time, calculated in
accordance with Subclause (1) is an amount involving a fraction of a
toea, the supplier may charge to the next
whole toea; and
(iii) Where aviation gasoline is supplied at a locality specified in
Column I of Schedule II, the maximum
surcharge for each aircraft specified in Column 2 of that Schedule
in relation to the locality concerned may be
charged by the supplier in addition to the maximum retail selling
price specified in Subclause (1).
3. SUPPLY TO GOVERNMENT.
Nothing in this Order applies to or relates to the supply of
aviation gasoline to the Government, to Australia
or to a Statutory Authority of the Government or of Australia.

                        PUBLIC SERVICE LAHARA SCHEME

                    APPLICATIONS FOR STUDY PLACES 1974-75
   There are two forms of study assistance available in this Scheme,
both are administered by the Public Service
Board's Training Section. The awards are known as Lahara Study
Places. The awards are available at the Univer-
sity of Papua New Guinea. (Teachers should apply for the Lahara
Session through the Department of Education as
in previous years.)
                                DIVISION A
Division A—Pre-matriculation Course
   Places in this Division will be strictly limited. Officers who
are awarded a place are advised that successful
completion of the Lahara Pre-matriculation Course does not provide
them with an educational qualification
of any type. No certificate is issued on successful completion of
the course. The course is only intended to serve
as a means of assessing the student's suitability for taking up
degree studies at the University. Officers applying
for places in Division A should only be those whose matriculation
status is not sufficient to commence degree
studies. (See also notes below.)
Eligibility
   Any permanent officer of the National Public Service.
                                DIVISION B

Division B—Degree Unit Courses
   This Division is intended to assist permanent officers of the
National Public Service who, through their
location or the nature of their duties have been prevented from
undertaking part-time University studies.
Eligibility
     (a) Permanent officers in the Port Moresby area who have
already completed part of their degree on
        a part-time basis.
     (b) Permanent officers transferred to Port Moresby within less
than one University of Papua New Guinea
        semester of application.
     (c) Permanent officers who are certified by their Department to
be prevented from undertaking part-
        time studies through the nature of their duties.
     (d) Permanent officers outside Port Moresby.


July, 1975                    2             Papua New Guinea Gazette

                  PUBLIC SERVICE LAHARA SCHEME—continued

        CONDITIONS APPLICABLE TO BOTH DIVISION A AND DIVISION B
Selection Criteria

    (a) Applicants must be acceptable to the Lahara Studies
Committee of the University of Papua New Guinea.
    (b) Departmental recommendation.
    (c) Service record.

Benefits

    (a)    Study leave with full pay.
    (b)    Fares will be paid where applicable for the officer (not his
family)
    (c)    A book allowance.
    (d)    Tuition and other compulsory fees are paid.

Duration

   A Lahara Study Place will apply only to the Lahara Session for
which it was granted. This generally covers
a period of six to eight weeks from 24th November to 16th January
1976. The successful completion of Lahara
studies does not give automatic entitlement to further studies
assistance,

Enrolment in Course

   Applicants for Lahara Study Places must ensure that at the time
of applying for this award they also apply
to the University for admission to the course. Enrolment forms are
available from University of Papua New
Guinea, Box 4820, University Post Office.

Closing Date

   The 15th August, 1975. Application Forms are available from the
Department of the Public Service Board's
Training Section but must be forwarded through the applicant's
Departmental Head to the Public Service Board,
Training Section, P.O. Ward Strip. Late applications will not be
accepted.

Gasoline.


     Made by the Price Controller under the provisions of the Prices
Regulations Act 1949, as amended to date,


to come into operation on the date of publication in the Government
Gazette.

1. REVOCATION.


     Prices Order No. 142 is hereby revoked.


2. DEFINITIONS.


     In this Order—


       "aviation gasoline" includes any substance normally sold as
aviation gasoline whether or not containing addi-


            tives of any kind;


       "supplier" in relation to aviation gasoline, means a person
or a firm who sells aviation gasoline for the


            purpose of consumption or use;


       "retail" means for the purpose of consumption or use,


3. MAXIMUM RETAIL PRICE.


      (i) where aviation gasoline is supplied at a locality
specified in Column 1 of Schedule I, the maximum price


per gallon at which the aviation gasoline may be supplied is the
maximum retail selling price specified in Column 2


of that Schedule in relation to the locality concerned; and

(ii) where the maximum price of any quantity of aviation
gasoline, supplied at any one time, calculated in


accordance with Subclause (i) is an amount involving a fraction of a
toea, the supplier may charge to the next


whole toea; and


     (iii) where aviation gasoline is supplied at a locality
specified in Column 1 of Schedule II, the maximum sur-


charge for each aircraft specified in Column 2 of that Schedule in
relation to the locality concerned may be


charged by the supplier in addition to the maximum retail selling
price specified in Subclause (i).


4. SUPPLY TO GOVERNMENT.


     Nothing in this Order applies to or relates to the supply of
aviation gasoline to the Government, to Australia


or to a Statutory Authority of the Government or of Australia.
