                  MAXIMUM PRICES FOR MANUFACTURED CIGARETTES
  MILTON FREDERICK ROBERTS, a Deputy Price Controller, by virtue of
the powers conferred by the Prices
  Regulation Act 1949, as amended to date, do hereby make the
following Order:—
                                PRICES ORDER No. 143
1. CITATION
   This Order may be cited as Prices Order No, 143.
2. COMMENCEMENT
   This Order shall come into operation on the date of publication
of this Order in the Gazette.
3. REVOCATION
   Prices Order No. 124 is hereby revoked.
4. DEFINITIONS
   In this Order—
     "cigarettes" means cigarettes which are manufactured in Papua
New Guinea from imported or locally
        grown tobacco leaf.
     "retail" means for the purpose of consumption or use.
5. MAXIMUM PRICE
   (a) The maximum price per packet at which cigarettes may be sold
by retail at any of the locations specified
in Schedule 1 is the amount specified in the Second Column of
Schedule 2 in relation to the brand and pack
specified opposite in the First Column of Schedule 2.
   (b) The maximum price per packet at which cigarettes may be sold
by retail at locations other than those
specified in Schedule 1 is the amount specified in the Third Column
of Schedule 2 in relation to the brand and
pack specified opposite in the First Column of Schedule 2.
6. DISPLAY OF PRICES
   A person or organisation who has in his custody or under his
control any of the cigarettes to which this Order
applies for sale by retail, or who offers, exhibits or exposes any
of those cigarettes for sale by retail, shall display
a ticket, label, placard or notice attached to or exhibited or
displayed with the cigarettes setting forth in a prominent
position in clear and legibe figures easily discernible to any
person inspecting suds cigarettes, the price at which the
cigarettes concerned may be bought.
7. MAXIMUM RETAIL PRICE OF CIGARETTES IN CERTAIN AREAS
   Notwithstanding anything in this Order, where a notice in writing
is given by the Controller to a supplier of
cigarettes fixing the maximum price at which cigarettes may be
supplied by him in any locality, being a price not
less than fixed by Clause 5 of this Order, the maximum price at
which cigarettes may be so supplied is the price
fixed in that Notice.

 PROHIBITION AND RESTRICTION OF SUPPLY, ETC., OF LIQUOR—MOUNT HAGEN
AND
                        KAGAMUGA
  THOMAS KINGSTON CRITCHLEY, High Commissioner, by virtue of the
powers conferred by Section 124 of the
 Liquor (Licensing) Act 1963, as amended to date, and all other
powers me enabling, and having received the
advice of the Executive Council, hereby restrict the sale, supply
and disposal of liquor in the towns of Mount Hagen
and Kagamuga for the period of the Mount Hagen Show, that is from
1st August, 1975 until 3rd August, 1975,

inclusive—
   (a) by prohibiting the sale, supply and disposal of liquor by the
holder of a restaurant licence except be-
      tween the hours of 12 noon and 1.30 p.m., and 7 p.m. and 9
p.m. when that liquor is part of a meal;
      and
   (b) by prohibiting the sale, supply and disposal of liquor by the
holder of any other licence or permit before
      5 p.m.

seventy-five.

THE PAPUA NEW GUINEA GOVERNMENT GAZETTE


THE Papua New Guinea Government Gazette is published sectionally in
accordance with the following arrange-

   ments set out below:


Public Service Gazette


     Public Service issue contains notices concerning vacancies,
transfers and promotions within the Papua New

Guinea Public Service. These issues are published monthly at 11.30
a.m. on the first Thursday of each month.


General Gazette


     General notices issue include the sittings of the House of
Assembly; Legislation (Acts assented to; Statutory

rules); Tenders etc. These issues are published weely at 11.30 a.m.
on Thursday.


Special Gazette

     Special issues are made on urgent matters as required. Single
copies are available on the day of issue at the

Government Printing Office at 10 toi a and are provided at no extra
charge with weekly issues.


Subscriptions

     Subscriptions are payable in advance. Rates are as follows:


     Within Papua New Guinea—including postage K15,00 per annum;
K7.50 per half year; K3.75 per quarter;

Australia—including postage K18.00 per annum; K9.00 per half
year; K4.50 per quarter;


     Overseas—including postage K55.00 per annum; K27.50 per half
year; K13.75 per quarter.


Notices


     "Notices for insertion" must be received at the Government
Printing Office, P.O. Box 3280, Port Moresby, be-

fore 11.30 a.m. on Friday preceding the day of publication excepting
the Public Service Board "Promotions and

Vacancies". Land Board advertisements must be lodged at 3 p.m. on
the afternoon preceding the normal closing

date.


     All notices, from whatever source, must have a covering
instruction setting out the publication details required.

The notice should be typewritten (double-spaced) on one side of the
paper only. Signatures in particular and

proper names must be shown very plainly in the text. Copy, not
submitted in accordance with these instructions,

will be returned unpublished.

THE Papua New Guinea Government Gazette is published sectionally in
accordance with the following arrange-

 ments set out below:


Public Service Gazette

  Public Service issue contains notices concerning vacancies,
transfers and promotions within the Papua New

Guinea Public Service. These issues are published monthly at 11.30
a.m. on the first Thursday of each month.


General Gazette

  General notices issue include the sittings of the House of
Assembly; Legislation (Acts assented to; Statutory

rules); Tenders etc. These issues are published weekly at 11.30 a.m.
on Thursday.


Special Gazette

  Special issues are made on urgent matters as required. Single
copies are available on the day of issue at the

Government Printing Office at 10 toea and are provided at no extra
charge with weekly issues.


Subscriptions

  Subscriptions are payable in advance. Rates are as follows:

  Within Papua New Guinea—including postage K15.00 per annum; K7.50
per half year; K3.75 per quarter;

  Australia—including postage K18.00 per annum; K9,00 per half year;
K4.50 per quarter;

  Overseas—including postage K55.00 per annum; K27.50 per half year;
K13.75 per quarter.


Notices

  "Notices for insertion" must be received at the Government
Printing Office, P.O. Box 3280, Port Moresby, be-

fore 11.30 a.m. on Friday preceding the day of publication excepting
the Public Service Board "Promotions and

Vacancies". Land Board advertisements must be lodged at 3 p.m. on
the afternoon preceding the normal closing

date.

  All notices, from whatever source, must have a covering
instruction setting out the publication details required.

The notice should be typewritten (double-spaced) on one side of the
paper only. Signatures in particular and

proper names must be shown very plainly in the text. Copy, not
submitted in accordance with these instructions,
will be returned unpublished.

                      PRICES ORDER No. 146

               A PRICES ORDER relating to the maximum retail price
for
                    MANUFACTURED CIGARETTES
MADE by a Deputy Price Controller under the provisions of the Prices
Regulation Act 1949, as amended to date, to
  come into operation on the date of publication in the Government
Gazette.
1. REVOCATION.
  Prices Order No. 143 is hereby revoked.
2. DEFINITIONS.
  In this Order—
   "cigarettes" means cigarettes which are manufactured in Papua New
Guinea from imported or locally grown
      tobacco leaf.
   "retail" means for the purpose of consumption or use.
3. MAXIMUM RETAIL PRICE.
   (a) The maximum price per packet at which cigarettes may be sold
by retail at any of the locations specified
      in Schedule 1 is the amount specified in the Second Column of
Schedule 2 in relation to the brand and
      pack specified opposite in the First Column of Schedule 2.
   (b) The maximum price per packet at which cigarettes may be sold
by retail at locations other than those
      specified in Schedule 1 is the amount specified in the Third
Column of Schedule 2 in relation to the
      brand and pack specified opposite in the First Column of
Schedule 2.
4. DISPLAY OF PRICES.
  A person or organisation who has in his custody or under his
control any of the cigarettes to which this Order
applies for sale by retail, or who, offers, exhibits or exposes any
of those cigarettes for sale by retail, shall display a
ticket, label, placard or notice attached to or exhibited or
displayed with the cigarettes setting forth in a prominent
position in clear and legible figures easily discernible to any
person inspecting such cigarettes, the price at which
the cigarettes concerned may be bought.

5. MAXIMUM RETAIL PRICE OF CIGARETTES IN CERTAIN AREAS.
  Notwithstanding anything in this Order, where a nctice in writing
is given by the Controller to a supplier of
cigarettes fixing the maximum price at which cigarettes may be
supplied by him in any locality, being a price not less
than fixed by Clause 3 of this Order, the maximum price at which
cigarettes may be so supplied is the price fixed in
that Notice.

                       PUBLIC NOTICE

                  EXERCISE OF MINISTERS' POWERS
TO-DAY is the date of commencement of the following Acts:—
    Constitutional Change (Consequential Provisions) (Amendment) Act
1975.
    Statute Law Revision (Ministers' Powers) Act 1975.
    Ministers' (Delegation) Act 1975.
THIS legislation affects the exercise of powers and functions by
Ministers. Where a Minister considers it desir-
  able that a person should be authorised to exercise one of his
powers and functions, the Minister may authorise
that person in one of the following ways:—
    (a) where the Minister has been given a statutory power of
delegation—by a formal instrument of
      delegation or subdelegation; or
    (b) where the Minister has not been given a statutory power of
delegation and the person to be authorised
      is an officer in a Department, branch, division or Office for
which the Minister is responsible — by an
      informal authorization (which may incidentally be embodied in
a departmental circular and be given
      by reference to office).
   For the time being the following Ministers have been given a
statutory power of delegation:—
    (a) all Ministers (in relation to entering into and executing
any Government contract or agreement).
    (b) the Minister for Transport and Civil Aviation (in relation
to the Civil Aviation (Interim Arrangements)
      Act 1973).
    (c) the Minister for Defence, Foreign Relations and Trade (in
relation to the Defence Act 1974.)
    (d) the Ministers responsible for the powers and functions
conferred by the Defence (Visiting Forces) Act
      1975).
    (e) the Minister for Education (in relation to any power or
function conferred on him by any law relating
      to education).
    (f) the Minister for Finance (in relation to the Electricity
Supply (Administration Power Stations) Act
      1970, the Port Moresby Water Supply Act, 1941 (Papua), the
Post and Telegraph (Finance) Act,
      1970 and the Stamp Duties Act, 1952).

The above powers of delegation also relate' to regulations and
certain other instruments made under the
specified Acts.
   The statutory powers of delegation referred to may be varied or
revoked by a regulation under the Ministers'
(Delegation) Act. Similarly other Ministers may be given a power of
delegation in relation to one or more
statutory powers or functions by the making of a regulation under
the Ministers' (Delegation) Act.
   Where a Minister has a power for delegation in relation to a
particular statutory power or function no person
(apart from the Minister) may exercise or perform that power or
function unless authorized by a formal instru-
ment of delegation. In relation to contracts and other transactions
with the Government the following classes of
persons are deemed to be delegates:—
    (a) financial delegates (up to the limit of the amount for which
they may approve requisitions):
    (b) procurement officers (up to the limit of the approved
requisition).

                        PRICES ORDER No. 149
A PRICES ORDER relating to the maximum retail price for—

                    PETROL, DISTILLATE AND LIGHTING
                             KEROSENE
   MADE by the Deputy Price Controller under the provisions of the
Prices Regulation Act 1949, as amended to
date, to come into operation on the date of publication in the
Government Gazette.

 1. CITATION.
   This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 149.

2. REVOCATION.
   The Prices Orders specified in Schedule 2 of this Order are
revoked.
3. DEFINITIONS.
   In this Order—
    "petrol" includes any substance normally sold as petrol whether
or not containing additives of any kind;
    "distillate" includes any substance normally sold as automotive
distillate whether or not containing additives
       of any kind;
    "kerosene" includes any substance normally sold as kerosene
being a medium refined petroleum product as
       used for lighting and cooking in home appliances, whether or
not containing additives of any kind;
    "wholesaler" in relation to petrol, distillate or lighting
kerosene means a person or a firm who sells petrol,
       distillate or lighting kerosene for the purpose of resale and
not for the purpose of use;

    "supplier" in relation to petrol, distillate or lighting
kerosene, means a person or a firm who sells petrol,
       distillate or lighting kerosene for the purpose of use;

       "retail" means for the purpose of consumption or use.

4. MAXIMUM PRICE.

   (i) Subject to Sub-Clause (II) of this Clause, where petrol,
distillate or lighting kerosene is supplied—
    (a) at a locality specified in the first Column of Schedule 1 to
this Order; or

    (b) at some other place at which the petrol, distillate or
lighting kerosene is transported from any such local-
       ity by or on behalf of a wholesaler or supplier;
the maximum price per gallon at which the petrol, distillate or
lighting kerosene may be supplied is the sum of—

    (c) the maximum retail selling price specified in the Second,
Third or Fourth Column as the case may be, of
       Schedule 1 in relation to the locality concerned; and

    (d) the amount (if any) charged for the transport referred to in
paragraph (b) of this Sub-Clause.
   (ii) Where the maximum price of any quantity of petrol,
distillate or lighting kerosene supplied at any one
time, calculated in accordance with Sub-Clause (i) of this Clause is
an amount involving a fraction of a toes, the sup-
plier may charge to the next whole toea.

5. SUPPLY TO GOVERNMENT ETC.
   Nothing in this Order applies to or relates to the supply of
petrol, distillate or lighting kerosene to the Gov-
ernment, Australia or a Statutory Authority of the Government or
Australia.

6. DISPLAY OF PRICES.
   A person or an organisation engaged in selling petrol, distillate
or lighting kerosene by retail shall display in each
of the places of business in prominent positions and in large, clear
and legible figures the maximum prices at which
such petrol, distillate or lighting kerosene may be bought.

Liquor (Licensing) Act 1963, as amended to date

          PROHIBITION AND RESTRICTION OF SUPPLY OF LIQUOR
I THOMAS KINGSTON CIUTCHLEY, High Commissioner, by virtue of the
powers conferred by Section 124 of
 /the Liquor (Licensing) Act 1963, as amended to date, and all other
powers me enabling, and having received
the advice of the Executive Council, hereby—
   (a) prohibit the supply of liquor by each holder of a dealer's
licence, storekeeper's licence and bottieshop
      licence, other than the supply of liquor by the holder of a
storekeeper's licence in respect of a Duty
      Free Shop, for the period 7th September, 1975 to 17th
September, 1975 (inclusive); and
   (b) prohibit the supply of liquor by each holder of a booth
licence, dinner permit, supper permit or special
      permit for the period 13th September, 1975 to 17th September,
1975 (inclusive); and
   (c) prohibit the supply of liquor by each holder of an occasional
licence, unless that holder has the prior
      written approval of the Chief Licensing Commissioner, for the
period of 13th September, 1975 to 17th
      September, 1975 (inclusive); and
   (d) prohibit the supply of liquor by each holder of a publican's
licence, tavern licence, canteen licence or
      club licence—
      (1) on 15th September, 1975, except between the hours of-
        12 noon and 2 p,m. (inclusive) and 4 p.m. and 6 p.m.
(inclusive); and
      (ii) on 16th September, 1975, except between the hours of-
        12 noon and 2 p.m. (inclusive) and 5 p.m. and 7 p.m.
(inclusive); and
      (iii) on 17th September, 1975, except between the hours of-
        12 noon and 2 p.m. (indusive) and 4 p.m. and 6 p.m.
(inclusive); and
   (e) notwithstanding anything in this notice each holder of a
publican's licence, limited hotel licence or res-
      idential dub licence may sell, supply and dispose of liquor on
licensed premises at any time to lodgers and
      their bona-fide guests within any guest lounge on the licensed
premises and lodgers room by waiter
      service; and
   (1)notwithstanding anything in this notice each holder of a
publican's licence, restaurant licence or limited
      hotel licence may sell, supply and dispose of liquor for
consumption in the dining room of the licensed
      premises to persons having a meal between the hours of 12 noon
and 2.30 p.m. (inclusive) and 6 p.m.
      and 10 p.m. (inclusive); and
   (g) prohibit the supply of liquor by each holder of a cabaret
permit for the period 13th September, 1975
      to 17th September, 1975 (indusive).
  Dated this twenty-ninth day of August, One thousand nine hundred

and seventy-five.
                                             T. K. CRITCHLEY,
                                              High Commissioner.

POLICY GUIDELINES UNDER SECTION 25
THE following guidelines within which the Commissioner shall operate
in the exercise and performance of his
  powers and functions under Part 111 of the Insurance Act 1974, as
in force from time to time, have been laid
down by the High Commissioner in Council:—


Papua New Guinea Gazette    3            No. 77-13th September, 1975

                        PRELIMINARY
1.—DEFINITIONS.
  For the purposes of these guidelines—
    "the Act" means the Insurance Act 1974, as in force from time to
time;
    "the applicant corporation" means a corporation that applies to
the Commissioner for a licence to carry on
      general insurance business under the Act.
                  QUALIFICATIONS FOR INSURERS
2.—FINANCIAL REQUIREMENTS.
  2.1. An application corporation shall be a public corporation.
  2.2. The minimum amount of shareholders' funds held by an
applicant corporation shall be K100,000.00.
  2.3. In addition to the deposit lodged under Section 26(1) of the
Act, the applicant corporation shall have
situated in Papua New Guinea, assets in excess of—
    (a) K100,000.00; or
    (b) 10 per centum of net premium income during the previous
financial year, whichever is the greater.
  2.4. The applicant corporation shall have assets in excess of
liabilities of K100,000.00 or 10 per centum of net
premium income in the previous year whichever is the greater.
3.—CALCULATION OF LIABILITIES AND ASSETS.
  3.1. For the purposes of paragraph 2.4, liabilities—
    (a) exclude-
      (i) shareholders' funds; and
      (ii) liabilities in respect of shareholders' funds; and
    (b) include contingent liabilities.
  3.2. For the purposes of paragraph 2.4 assets exclude in tangible
assets, including expenses of the applicant
corporation in relation to the formation, extension or purchase of
its business or the purchase of goodwill.
4.—INFORMATION MAY BE REQUIRED.
  The Commissioner may require the applicant corporation to provide
information with respect to—
    (a) the value of an asset of that corporation; and
    (b) any other matter that the Commissioner considers necessary.
5.—ARRANGEMENTS FOR RE-INSURANCE.
  The applicant corporation shall make arrangements approved by the
Commissioner for re-insurance of liabilities
in respect of risks against which persons are, or are to be, insured
in the course of its general insurance business.
6.—ADMINISTRATION OF APPLICANT CORPORATION.
  The conduct of the business of an insurer shall he controlled by a

person experienced in general insurance busi-
ness.
                  QUALIFICATIONS FOR BROKERS
7.—BROKERS.
  The Commissioner may require a broker when making his application
for a licence to provide information
that—
    (a) he is a person of good fame and character; and
    (b) he is experienced and competent to carry on the business of
a broker; and
    (c) he has a suitable financial record; and
    (d) he is covered by a professional indemnity policy of
insurance to a cover of not less than 1(75,000.00.
              QUALIFICATIONS FOR INSURERS AND BROKERS
8.—TRAINING PROGRAMME, ETC.
  8.1.—Training of Personnel.
  Every licensed insurer and broker shall make arrangements approved
by the Commissioner for a programme of
employment and training of Papua New Guinean personnel in the
industry.
  8.2.—Utilization of Locally Owned Services,
  Every licensed insurer and broker shall, where available—
    (a) utilize insurance and other facilities of Papua New Guinea;
and
    (b) give preference to Papua New Guinean owned facilities.
9.—NOTIFICATION OF AGREEMENTS INVOLVING FOREIGN EXCHANGE.
  9.1. Every licensed insurer and broker shall provide the
Commissioner with particulars concerning—
    (a) an existing agreement; and
    (b) a proposed agreement,
in relation to Papua New Guinea business, involving foreign exchange
to which he is a party.
  9.2. A licensed insurer or broker shall not enter into an
agreement under Section 9.1(b) unless the prior
approval in writing of the Commissioner has been obtained.
  Dated the twenty-seventh day of August, One thousand nine hundred
and seventy-five.

                 THE PAPUA NEW GUINEA NATIONAL GAZETTE
 The Papua New Guinea National Gazette is published sectionally in
accordance with the following arrangements set
out below.
THE PUBLIC SERVICES ISSUE.
   The Public Services Issue contains notices concerning vacancies,
transfers and promotions within the National
Public Service. These issues are published monthly in the first week
of each month.
   Single copies may be obtained from the Government Printing
Office, Muruk Haus, Kumul Avenue, Waigani, for
K2.00 each.
THE GENERA.L NOTICES ISSUE.
   The General Notices Issue includes the date of the sittings of
the National Parliament; Legislation (Acts assented to,
Statutory Rules); Tenders etc. These issues are published weekly at
11.30 a.m. on Thursday.
   Single copies may be obtained from the above address for K2.00.
SPECIAL ISSUES.
   Special Issues are made on urgent matters as required. They are
provided at no extra cost to subscribers.
   Single copies may be purchased on the day of issue at the above
address at the prices shown above for respective
issues.
SUBSCRIPTIONS.

NOTICES FOR GAZETTAL.
   Notice for insertion in the General Gazette must be received at
the Government Printing Office, P.O. Box 1280,
Port Moresby, before 12.00 noon on Friday, preceding the day of
publication.
   All notices for whatever source, must have a covering instruction
setting out the publication details required.
   The notice must be an original. Photostat or carbon copies are
not accepted.
   The notice should be typewritten (double-spaced) and one side of
the paper only. Signatures in particular, and
proper names must be shown clearly in the text.
   Copies submitted not in accordance with these instructions will
be returned unpublished.
PROCEDURES FOR GOVERNMENTAL SUBSCRIPTIONS.
   Departments are advised that to obtain the Gazettes they must
send their requests to:
   (i) The Government Printing Office, P.O. Box 1280, Port Moresby,
National Capital District.

required to pay all printing charges under the
instructions from the Manual of Financial Procedures Section 13.3,
Subsection 11.

                        REQUIREMENTS)
I, PAULUS AIN, Commissioner & Chief Executive Officer, by virture of
the powers conferred by Section 114(1) of
the Independent Consumer and Competition Commission Act 2002 hereby
propose to publish in the National Gazette
a notice under Section 108(5) of the Independent Consumer and
Competition Commission Act 2002 in substantially the
same form and substance as indicated in the draft below, declaring
the goods described in the Notice to be unsafe in
Papua New Guinea.

SECTION 108(5) DECLARATION (FOOD PRODUCT LABELLE':rG REQUIREYFFNTS)
I, PAULUS AIN, Commissioner & Chief Executive Officer, by virture of
the powers conferred by Section 108(5) of
the Independent Consumer and Competition Commission Act 2002 and all
other enabling powers, hereby declares as
unsafe in Papua New Guinea, the following goods (and similar
products) that fail to comply with these labellino-

requirements under the Food Sanitation Regulation 2007, Food
Sanitation Act 1991 and the Packaging Act 1974:

   1. Any word, statement, information or direction that is required
to appear as a label on a package or
      apparatus shall—
      (a) in the case of infant formula requiring reconstitution, be
in English;
      (1) any imported food specifically packaged for export to
Papua New Guinea, be in English;
      (c) in the case of imported food and food additives other than
those prescribed in Paragraph (a) and
          (b), be in English.; and
          in the case of food and food additives produced, prepared,
manufactured, processed or packed in
          Papua New Guinea, be in English;

      A packer who packs an article shall ensure the pack containing
the article is marked in the prescribed
      manner with a statement in English of the true weight or
measure of the article.
   3. Any package or apparatus containing food or food additives for
sale shall bear on or attached to it a label
      containing a statement in English that identifies the country
in which the food or food addictive was made
      or produced; and

     4. Any package or apparatus containing food or food additives
for sale shall bear on or attached to it a label
         containing a description in English of the same and address
of the vendor, manufacturer, packer or
         importer that includes the name, road or street, road or
street number, locality and country, and business
         hours telephone contact number.
    All labelling requirements mentioned above must be present on
the label of any package or apparatus containing
food products. Partial non-compliance of this Notice is deemed as
non-compliance.

    Nothing in this Notice shall   limit the product labelling and
other requirements under Section   12(1)(a) to (i)
and Section 12(3) to (11) of the   Food Sanitation Regulation 2007,
the Food Sanitation Act 1991 and   the Packaging
Act 1974, and the obligations of   the supplier of goods to comply
with them.

Exemptions:

    (a) Provided labelling complies with the above, labelling in
other languages may also appear on packaging or
         apparatus.

    (b) Food that is prepared or offered for immediate consumption
in catering establishments, restaurants,
         canteens, schools, hospitals and other institutions where
the product is accompanied by sufficient
         information in English in relation to that product to
enable the purchaser to determine the content of that
         particular product before purchasing it.

    (c) Provided labelling complies with the above, labelling in
the form of a sticker placed on the product to
         reflect any one or more of the labelling requirements not
stated on the product packaging or apparatus is
         adequate for the duration of this Notice.

    Summary of Reasons:

    Products that are incorrectly labelled may pose a risk to the
safety of consumers. Consumers may not recognize
ingredients that may cause an allergic reaction or may misinterpret
warnings or instructions that accompany the
products. Also they may not understand directions for food
preparations or storage that appear on the packaging or
apparatus.

    Subject to the above, any person or persons supplying food
products that do not comply with the above
labelling requirements may be in breach of this Notice and Section
108(1) of the Independent Consumer and
Competition Commission Act 2002, and may be liable to a penalty of
up to K100, 000.00 or imprisonment of up to 2
3 ears, if found guilty by the court. Further, pursuant to Section
111(1) of the Independent Consumer and Competition
Commission Act 2002, action maybe taken by the Independent Consumer
and Competition Commission to recall these
products. The Independent Consumer and Competition Commission
therefore advises that these products should not
be supplied in Papua New Guinea.

    This Notice supercides the Notice published in the National
Gazette No. G14 on the 16th January, 2018

of this Notice in the National Gazette, if that' wish
for the Independent Consumer and Competition Commission to bold a
conference in relation to this Notice.

I, PAULUS AIN, Commissioner & Chief Executive Officer, by virtue of

         SECTION 108(5) DECLARATION (CERTAIN UNSAFE BABY WALKERS)


I, PAULUS AIN, Commissioner & Chief Executive Officer, by virtue of
the powers conferred by Section 108(5) of
the Independent Consumer and Competition Commission Act 2002 and all
the enabling powers, hereby declares as
unsafe in Papua New Guinea baby walkers of the type described in
this Notice. A baby walker for the purpose of this
Notice is an infant and nursery product which consists of a frame on
wheels designed to support a child whilst the
child's feet are touching the ground for infants and babies who are
learning to walk. The product is propelled by the
movement of the child on the wheels or castors.


    Such baby walkers cannot be supplied in PNG unless the baby
walker:


    1. is stable;
    2. has an adequate braking mechanism (and in assessing 1 and 2
we will have regard to the product

Summary of Reasons

Such baby walkers create instances of injury or death where:

            the baby walker falls down stairs or off an elevated
area, resulting in possible head injuries;
            the baby walker is unstable and tips over also resulting
in potential injury;
            the child in the baby walker gains access to hazardous
areas, products or objects which can cause
            injuries such as burns, electrocution, cuts and other
wounds; and
        • the child can potentially be able to get out of the baby
walker resulting in possible falls anywhere,

and have the potential to be unsafe.

imprisonment of up to 2 years, if found guilty by the court.

Competition Commission Act 2002 action may
be taken by the Independent Consumer and Competition Commission to
recall these products. The Independent
Consumer and Competition Commission therefore advises that these
products should not be supplied in Papua New
Guinea.

                      LAND AVAILABLE FOR LEASING
A. APPLICANT:
  Applicants or Tenderers should note-
    1. Full name (block letters), occupation and address;
    2. If a Company, the proper Registered Company name and address
of the Company representative;
    3. If more than one person, the tenancy desired and, if tenancy
in common, the division of shares.
  Applicants or tenderers should note-
    4, That a lease cannot be held in a name registered under the
Business Names Act only; and
    5. That in the case of death in joint tenancy, the deceased
partner's interest vests in the surviving partner and,
     in the case of tenancy in common, the deceased partner's
interest vests in his estate.
B. TYPE OF LEASE:
  Leases provided for a Business, Residence, Pastoral, Agricultural,
Mission or Special Purposes. State Leases may be
granted for a maximum period of 99 years. Applicants should note
that, in the case of land within physical planning areas
the purpose of the lease must be in accordance with the zoning
requirements of the Physical Planning Act.
C. PROPOSED PURPOSES, IMPROVEMENTS, ETC:
  The applicant or tenderer should provide fullest details (on
attachment if necessary) of his proposal for the lease
including information on-
    1. Financial status or prospects;
    2. Details of other land holdings in Papua New Guinea including
approximate value of improvements to these
     holdings;

3. Approximate value and type of proposed improvements to the
land applied for;
    4. Experience and abilities to develop the land;
    5. Any other details which would support the application.

A. APPLICANT:
     Applicants or Tenderers should note-
         1. Full name (block letters), occupation and address;
         2. If a Company, the proper Registered Company name and
address of the Company representative;
         3. If more than one person, the tenancy desired and, if
tenancy in common, the division of shares.
     Applicants or tenderers should note-
         4. That a lease cannot be held in a name registered under
the Business Names Act only; and
         5. That in the case of death in joint tenancy, the deceased
partner's interest vests in the surviving partner and, in the case
of tenancy
            in common, the deceased partner's interest vests in his
estate.
B. TYPE OF LEASE:
     Leases provided for a Business, Residence, Pastoral,
Agricultural, Mission or Special Purposes. State Leases may be
granted for a maximum period
of 99 years. Applicants should note that, in the case of land within
physical planning areas the purpose of the lease must be in
accordance with the zoning
requirements of the Physical Planning Act.
C. PROPOSED PURPOSES, IMPROVEMENTS, ETC:
     The applicant or tenderer should provide fullest details (on
attachment if necessary) of his proposal for the lease including
information on-
         1. Financial status or prospects;
         2. Details of other land holdings in Papua New Guinea
including approximate value of improvements to these holdings;
         3. Approximate value and type of proposed improvements to
the land applied for;
         4. Experience and abilities to develop the land;
         5. Any other details which would support the application.
D. DESCRIPTION OF LAND:
     To be used only when NOT in response to an advertisement. A
brief description giving area and locality is required. A sketch
plan should
be provided on an attachment. Where possible the land parcel should
be identified on a map published by the Department of Lands &
Physical Planning.
     In the case of Tenders or an advertisement of land available
for leasing the description is to be inserted in the column provided
under the heading
"Tender or Land Available Preference".
E. TENDER OF LAND AVAILABLE PREFERENCE:
     The preference should be clearly indicated. In cases where
there are more than 20 preferences the additional preferences may be
shown on attach-

ment. The "Description" should give the Lot and Section number or
the Portion number as shown in the Gazette. The "Amount Offered"
column need
only be completed in the case of tenders.
F TENDERERS:
      Tenderers should take particular note that a tender for an
amount less than the reserve price is invalid and shall not be
considered. The
successful tenderer will be required to pay the full amount of the
tender.

an applicant or tenderer for a Town Subdivision Lease shall submit:

subdivision.

installation of roads and drainage.

     Consolidated Contractors (PNG) Limited, a contracting company
to the PNG LNG PROJECT wishes to engage
the services of skilled and experienced non-citizens who are
required urgently in the Construction Phase of the LNG
Project. The company is engaged in the construction of Komo Airfield
in Southern Highlands and the LNG Main Plant
Buildings at the Motukea Site, Port Moresby.

     The exemptions granted in accordance to Section 51 of the
Employment of Non-Citizens Act 2007 are always in
the interest of the nation and for a good cause, in view of the
PROJECT'S contribution to the country's development
in terms of economic, human resource and infrastructure development.

        The exemptions are granted from 17th March 2012 to 17th March
2013.

        Specific conditions placed against the exemptions are:-

      (1) For the company to pay a fee of K1000.00 for each employee
to the Department of Labour & Industrial
            Relations;

      (2) For the company to register all non-citizen employees that
require registration with a professional body;
      (3) For the company to provide employment opportunities

(decent work, fair pay, promotions etc.) to citizen
            workers;
      (4) For the company to provide opportunities for human
resource development and skills training to its
            employees.
      (5) Non English speaking countries to show evidence of English
proficiency for applicants.

     March 2012.


Hon. Martin Aini, MP.,

Minister for Labour and Industrial Relations.
